name: flrh-agent-runtime-boundary
purpose: Evaluate whether deterministic functional, logic, reactive, harness, and typed-graph mechanics justify a reusable agent runtime boundary.
rationale: Bounded sibling Python reference slices exist for pure F, ground stratified L, supplied-value scalar-frontier R, and one stateless direct L-to-R projection; no integrated runtime or production consumer exists yet.
Durability, recovery, effect reconciliation, and graph interoperability are specified but unmeasured.
Direct L-to-R projection is measured while the engine verdict remains defer

boundary.owns: Deterministic transition, fixpoint, unit-delta stabilization, and typed stable-proposal output
boundary.mechanism: Compute a stable FLR transition from explicit snapshots, events, rule bundles, and dataflow profiles while H alone binds policy, capability, approval, intent, commit, and effects
boundary.state_authority: A future fenced H store would own accepted state; the current repository owns specifications, stateless pure-F, pure-L, and pure-R reference functions, and one stateless direct L-to-R projection only

contract: evaluate(snapshot, accepted_event, rule_bundle, dataflow_profile) -> StableTransitionAndEffectProposals | TypedRejection
invariants: Identical explicit inputs and versions produce identical canonical output.
F, L, and R never execute external effects.
R never publishes a reaction batch before the logical frontier passes.
Unknown external outcomes require reconciliation before retry or terminal success.
failure_model: Malformed or incompatible inputs yield typed rejection without mutation.
Non-convergent logic or dataflow reaches a bounded pathology outcome.
Checkpoint or version incompatibility fails closed.
Evidence gaps prevent terminal success rather than being inferred away.
verification: Property tests compare replay and worklist-order invariance.
Incremental insert, delete, and retract results match clean full recomputation.
Crash injection covers intent commit, dispatch, external success, receipt, and reconciliation boundaries.
Resolved production and harness composition graphs differ only by approved adapter substitutions.

promotion_gates.criterion: Two named independent consumers use the same narrow-waist contract for three compatible version cycles.
prerequisites: Name and operate two independent consumers before adoption evidence is counted.

promotion_gates.criterion: Replay is byte-stable in two clean processes and incremental results equal clean recomputation.
prerequisites: Use the measured M3 corpus as one input, use the measured direct L-to-R projection, and demonstrate persistent incremental reuse before closing the incremental metric.

promotion_gates.criterion: Fenced writing, checkpoint compatibility, recovery, cancellation, schema migration, and effect reconciliation are demonstrated operational requirements in real consumers.
prerequisites: Operate real consumers with durable H control before classifying requirements as demonstrated.

promotion_gates.criterion: M0 through M5 pass with durable receipts and the frozen crash matrix produces no duplicate confirmed mutations.
prerequisites: Freeze the M4 crash matrix before executing recovery trials.

promotion_gates.criterion: Ingress, queues, deadlines, backpressure, cancellation, timeout, schema evolution, capabilities, and observability meet preregistered numeric limits.
prerequisites: Preregister one numeric limit and measurement procedure for every listed operational dimension before M6 evaluation.

promotion_gates.criterion: Policy variation remains outside the shared mechanism without core forks.
prerequisites: Exercise at least two independent consumer policy profiles.

promotion_gates.criterion: A frozen comparison shows less duplicated state and coordination than separate modules without exceeding the registered fault-rate margin.
prerequisites: Preregister the duplication metric, task corpus, and fault-rate noninferiority margin before comparison.

falsifiers: Real tasks repeatedly require ambient effects inside the deterministic kernel.
Incremental results fail to converge to clean recomputation.
Planned consumers require incompatible semantics rather than shared adapters.
The boundary adds more coordination and state than it removes.
